title: `ObjectView` is a third, drifted reader of the `filter[...]` URL family: an operator suffix is swallowed into the FIELD NAME instead of being dropped
body:
Found while fixing objectui#8883 (dev seat). Filed rather than folded in: different file, different package, and objectui#8883's ruling scopes it to the reference rail.

## The measurement

`ObjectView` is the component behind `/apps/:appName/:objectName` (`packages/app-shell/src/console/AppContent.tsx:999`), and it parses the `filter[...]` URL family with its OWN reader:

```
packages/app-shell/src/views/ObjectView.tsx:2092-2098
    const m = /^filter\[(.+)\]$/.exec(key);
    if (m && m[1] && value !== '') out.push([m[1], '=', value]);
```

The `(.+)` is GREEDY, so an operator-suffixed key does not fail to match — it matches with the suffix swallowed into the FIELD NAME. Both parsers of this URL family were run on the same three inputs, verbatim copies of the shipped functions, in one command:

| input | `drillUrlFilters.parseUrlFilterTriples` (the ADR-0055 `/data` surface) | `ObjectView.urlFilters` |
|---|---|---|
| `filter[owners][contains]=u1` | `[]` — dropped, as its docblock promises | `[["owners][contains","=","u1"]]` |
| lit control `filter[owners]=u1` | `[["owners","=","u1"]]` | `[["owners","=","u1"]]` |
| lit control `filter[amount][gte]=100` | `[["amount",">=","100"]]` | `[["amount][gte","=","100"]]` |

Both non-empty-but-wrong readings and the one empty reading sit beside a lit control in the same run, so neither is an unmeasured cell.

⇒ On `/apps/:app/:object`, `?filter[amount][gte]=100` does not filter by a range and does not fall back to no condition either: it emits a condition on a field named `amount][gte`, which no object declares. What the backend then does with a condition on a nonexistent column is the user-visible symptom, and it is not "the range was ignored".

## Why this is a defect and not a style note

`drillUrlFilters`' own docblock states the contract this diverges from, and states the reason the module exists:

> Keeping both sides in ONE module keeps the `filter[field][op]` operator contract (#1752) from drifting between the code that emits a URL and the code that parses it back.

`ObjectView` is a THIRD reader of the same param family that never joined that module, and it has drifted: it neither implements the operator arm nor rejects it. The `/data` surface's deliberate "ignore an unknown suffix, never silently downgrade to equality" posture is exactly what `ObjectView` fails to do.

## Reachability, measured — latent today, not unreachable

No producer in the repo emits an operator-suffixed `filter[...]` key to this route: `useOpenRecordList.ts:88` navigates to `/:objectName/data` (the correct parser), and `serializeDrillFilterParams` is only reached from there. So nothing in-app walks into it today.

It is reachable by a hand-written or bookmarked URL, and these URLs are an ADDRESSABLE public surface by design — that is the whole premise of ADR-0055 and of #1752's operator contract. A user who copies the range spelling from the `/data` surface onto the plain object route gets a silently wrong query rather than a refusal.

## Deliberately NOT claimed here

Whether the repair is "make `ObjectView` call `parseUrlFilterTriples`" or "make it REFUSE an operator suffix it cannot execute" is not asserted. The first is the obvious one-reader fix and would give the plain object route range operators it has never had — a behaviour addition, which is why it wants a ruling rather than a patch. objectui#9159 is a different gap on the same family (the `/data` dialect has no is-null operator) and does not cover this.
